elements.element: Transition assistance is triggered by both expiry and termination.
elements.evidence: The clause applies only on the Servicer's “resignation or termination”; it does not address expiry.

elements.element: The Vendor must provide post-termination transition assistance.
elements.evidence: The Servicer must cooperate in an orderly transition and “provide such transition assistance.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for up to 6 months after the applicable trigger.
elements.evidence: The clause requires assistance for at least 90 days but does not commit the Servicer to provide assistance through a six-month period.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be provided at the Vendor's then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no rates or compensation provision for transition assistance.

elements.element: The Vendor must return Customer Data to the Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause requires delivery of Receivable Files and maintained accounts and records to the Successor Servicer, not return of all Customer Data to the Customer; it also preserves broad transfer restrictions.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned within 30 days after the applicable trigger.
elements.evidence: For the covered resignation-or-termination events, the clause requires delivery of the Receivable Files and maintained accounts and records within 30 days. Coverage of expiry is assessed separately.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No machine-readable or other required export format is specified.

elements.element: The Vendor must certify deletion of Customer Data after returning it.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no deletion or deletion-certification obligation.

elements.element: Transition assistance is triggered by both expiry and termination.
elements.evidence: The obligation is triggered by resignation or termination, with no express coverage of expiry.

elements.element: The Vendor must provide post-termination transition assistance.
elements.evidence: The Servicer expressly must “provide such transition assistance” in connection with the orderly transition.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be provided for 90 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires transition assistance for “at least ninety (90) days,” which meets the 90-day minimum.

elements.element: The Vendor must export the relevant data.
elements.evidence: The Servicer must deliver the Receivable Files and its maintained accounts and records to the Successor Servicer, although the existing transfer-restriction carve-outs remain.

elements.element: The data export must occur within 30 days after the applicable trigger.
elements.evidence: For the covered resignation-or-termination events, delivery is expressly required within 30 days. The omission of expiry is assessed in the separate trigger element.

result.reason: The redline adds the fallback durations but does not cover expiry, so neither complete position is satisfied. It also changes the timing for transfer of funds—an unrelated commercial obligation—from “as soon as practicable” to 30 days. Applying that fixed deadline to funds “later received” is defective because funds received after day 30 cannot be transferred within 30 days after termination. The preferred six-month period, then-current rates, machine-readable format, and deletion certification are absent.
